slides.subline: Single-use plastic is banned inside Korean cafes. Paper is not — and the government is drafting that ban for the third time

slides.title:
The cup depends
on where you drink it.
slides.body:
One line in the resource-saving law decides what you are handed. Food-service businesses may not use single-use plastic cups for customers drinking in. Sit down and the drink has to arrive in something reusable — a mug, a glass, a steel tumbler. The penalty runs to 3 million won.

Take the same drink out of the door and the rule stops applying. That is why staff ask, and why the answer changes the cup.

The one hole in it is paper. A matching ban on in-store paper cups was written in November 2022, given a year's grace, and then withdrawn in November 2023 to spare small operators. Paper has been unrestricted ever since.

slides.cta:
Staying or going?
Save this before you order

caption:
In a Korean cafe, one question decides what your drink arrives in. Staying or going?

The resource-saving law bars food-service businesses from using single-use plastic cups for customers drinking on the premises. Sit down and it has to be a mug, a glass or a reusable tumbler; the fine reaches 3 million won. Walk out with it and the rule no longer applies. That is the whole logic behind the question at the till.

Paper is the gap. A matching ban on in-store paper cups was written in November 2022, given a year's grace period, then withdrawn in November 2023 to spare small operators — so paper has been unrestricted ever since, and plenty of places quietly use it.

That may not last. On 10 August 2026 the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment told the president it wants the plastic rule extended to paper, phased in from larger shops first. Thresholds of 33㎡ or 100㎡ are being discussed and the ministry has promised standards and a timetable within the year. Nothing is final yet.

Something did change in September. Twenty-three brands and around 150 independent cafes — roughly 22,000 shops, Ediya and Starbucks and Paris Baguette among them — signed an agreement with the ministry in July that took effect in September: reusable cups for anyone drinking in, paper included; no double-cupping; straws only if you ask. Bring your own cup and you can save up to 800 won, 300 to 400 of it off the price and the rest in government carbon points.

Scale, for context: those franchise groups still got through 1.09 billion disposable cups in 2025, up 1.6% on the year.

One more thing if you are in Jeju. The 300-won cup deposit still runs there; you get it back when you return the cup, and 60% of them came back last year.

Sources on the last slide. Research, not a visit, and no venue recommended here.
